editorial:
Imagine spending a week at a gorgeous Greek villa with a bunch of rich, bored Brits. That is exactly what you get here. You will see the Skidmore family and their fancy friends lounging by infinity pools, wearing expensive clothes, and eating five-star meals. The whole vibe is super relaxed and sunny at first, but there is a catch. This group has a weird tradition of playing mean pranks on each other just to stay entertained. It starts out as lighthearted fun, but you can tell that the tension is building up under the surface as they try to one-up each other.

What really makes this work is how the mood shifts when the big master prank goes totally wrong. The acting is spot on, making you laugh at how ridiculous these privileged people are when things fall apart. While the middle part slows down a bit, the chaotic ending makes up for it. If you want a movie that feels like a wild vacation gone wrong, you should definitely check this out. It looks stunning, so you should stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection to really see those Greek landscapes.
endingExplained: The big prank backfires when a fake crime scene becomes way too real, leading the group to believe someone has actually died. The twist is that the person they thought was dead was just hiding to scare them. However, the panic causes them to accidentally destroy the villa and reveal their deepest secrets. In the end, they are left broke and embarrassed, proving that their mean games finally caught up with them.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark comedies about rich people losing control.
